What's new in Callout 0.7.5

Version 0.7.5 Alpha

0.7.5 does one thing: the crosshair now appears only while you are selecting a region to capture. After the capture, over the Card, the pointer is the ordinary arrow with the tool’s badge riding on it — not a crosshair. Since August every drawing tool had put its badge on a crosshair, so the moment a Card landed under the pointer the crosshair was back; with the capture crosshair lost and found twice in 0.7.4, that became impossible to unsee. The text tool keeps its I-beam, and hovering anything you drew still shows the hand.

Nothing else changed. If you are reading this in the update window, that is the point: small fixes arrive as soon as they exist.

Fixed

  • The crosshair belongs to capture. It is the pointer while you drag out a region, and nowhere else. On the Card the tool badge now rides on the arrow, exactly where it always sat, so where a click lands does not move.

What's new in Callout 0.7.4

Version 0.7.4 Alpha

0.7.4 answers the first round of notes on the updater and the crosshair. Callout now checks for updates every time it launches, and every hour while it is running — it was checking once a day, so quitting and relaunching to pick up a new build did nothing if you had checked in the last twenty-four hours, which several of you noticed. And you now decide when it looks: Settings → General has an Updates section with three checkboxes. The crosshair 0.7.3 said it had brought back was only there while the mouse was moving — hold still and it fell back to an arrow. It is now drawn by Callout itself over an invisible system cursor, so it is there whether you move or not. And something only a brand-new tester would ever see: if Callout does not yet have Screen Recording permission and you press the capture hotkey, the alert explaining what to do now comes to the front. Since 0.7.2 it could open behind the app you were using — so it looked as if nothing had happened at all.

Nothing else changed. If you are reading this in the update window, that is the point: small fixes now arrive as soon as they exist.

Fixed

  • Quit and relaunch, and Callout checks for an update. It was checking at most once a day, which is the normal habit for a finished app and the wrong one for an alpha that ships several builds a week. It now checks a few seconds after every launch and once an hour while it runs. Nothing about what it sends changed: one request for the release list, carrying the version and nothing else.
  • You decide when it looks. Settings → General → Updates has three checkboxes — When Callout opens, Every hour while it runs, Once a day. Tick any combination, or none at all; Help → Check for Updates… works whatever you choose. All three start on. If you had switched the old single checkbox off, all three start off.
  • The crosshair stays put. 0.7.3 restored it, but only while the mouse was moving — macOS lets the app in front reassert its own cursor the moment you hold still, and Callout deliberately stays out of front so your open menus survive. The fix that actually holds was found by photographing the pointer rather than reasoning about it: the system cursor is made invisible over the capture overlay and Callout draws the crosshair itself, exactly at the pointer. If you ever see an arrow as well, tell me — that would be new.
  • Holding Space to move the selection is guarded. If something takes the keyboard away from the capture overlay mid-drag, the drag keeps working but Space silently stops — we reproduced that exactly. The overlay now takes the keyboard back the moment it loses it, and writes down who took it. If Space ever fails to move the box for you, use Help → Report a Bug… straight afterwards: the report will name the culprit.
  • The Screen Recording alert comes to the front. Callout stays out of the way of the app you are capturing — that is what lets an open menu survive the capture — and the one time it must step forward is to tell you it has no permission. It now does.

What's new in Callout 0.7.3

Version 0.7.3 Alpha

0.7.3 is a small release with one job: put the crosshair back. In 0.7.2 the capture overlay learned to stay out of the way of whatever app you were using — which is what lets you capture an open menu — and the crosshair cursor was a casualty of that change. It is back, and it stays for the whole gesture.

It is also the first release that arrives on its own. If you are reading this in the update window, the mechanism 0.7.2 promised has just worked: no email, no download, no dragging. Install and Relaunch, and you are done.

Fixed

  • The crosshair is back during capture. 0.7.2 changed the capture overlay so that the app you were working in stays in front (that is what lets a menu stay open while you capture it), and macOS only honours an app’s cursor while that app is in front — so the crosshair fell back to a plain arrow. The overlay now asks for its cursor in the way macOS provides for exactly this case, and re-asserts it as the mouse moves. Nothing else about capture changed.
